deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is Gauss's working sheet for his second elements of Vesta. Olbers discovered Vesta on 29 March 1807. The page has three parts: (I) the elements; (II) the reduction of the elements to Gauss's equatorial constants (Theoria Motus arts. 50–57, same method), ending in ready-to-use formulas giving equatorial heliocentric coordinates as functions of the eccentric anomaly; (III) two solar places (12 and 16 May 1807) from solar tables. These continue the April/May solar places on the previous page and supply the ephemeris or orbit comparison. The previous page fixes the obliquity eps = 23°27'49.98".

(I) ELEMENTS (Braunschweig, mean equinox, epoch 1807 Mar 29.5).
- Mean longitude L0 = 192°10'11.056".
- Daily tropical mean motion n_trop = 980.70675".
- Tropical period = 1296000/980.70675 = 1321.496 d. Correct.
- 'Sonnenferne' (aphelion) longitude = 69°58'9.10". Hence the perihelion longitude is pi = 249°58'9.10".
- e = 0.08722304.
- log a = 0.3723521, so a = 2.356961.
- Ascending node Omega = 103°18'50.86"; inclination i = 7°8'6.82".
- Marginal note: nutation 17.12".
- [Mine] log a follows from Kepler's third law with the sidereal motion n_sid = n_trop - 50.2"/365.25 ≈ 980.5693" and Gauss's constant k = 3548.18761": log a = (2/3)(log k - log n_sid) = 0.3723523. Agreement is to 2e-7.

(II) CONSTANTS FOR EQUATORIAL COORDINATES. Let u = v + omega, where omega = pi - Omega = 146°39'18.24". The coordinates are:
- x = r sin a sin(A+u)
- y = r sin b sin(B+u)
- z = r sin c sin(C+u)

These constants are defined by:
- sin a sin A = cos Omega; sin a cos A = -sin Omega cos i
- sin b sin B = sin Omega cos eps; sin b cos B = cos Omega cos i cos eps - sin i sin eps
- sin c sin C = sin Omega sin eps; sin c cos C = cos Omega cos i sin eps + sin i cos eps

Column 1 (A, a):
- log cos i = 9.9966236; log|tan Omega| = 0.6258928; their sum is 0.6225164 = log|tan Omega cos i|.
- tan A = -1/(tan Omega cos i). Both sin a sin A and sin a cos A are negative, so A is in the third quadrant: A = 193°24'51.48".
- sin a = cos Omega / sin A: 9.3622745 - 9.3654706 = 9.9968040 ('sin a').
- cos a = sin i sin Omega: 9.0941621 + 9.9881674 = 9.0823295.

Column 2 (auxiliary angles):
- log tan i = 9.0975384; log|cos Omega| = 9.3622745.
- tan psi = tan i / cos Omega: log = 9.7352639, giving psi = 151°28'20.5". The transcription's 151°28'10.48" cannot be right, since psi + eps is written 174°56'10.48".
- tan psi2 = tan i cos Omega: log = 8.4598129, giving psi2 = 178°20'55.47", and psi2 + eps = 201°48'45.45". [My interpretation] This second angle is used for cos b and cos c.
- log(cot Omega cos i) = 9.3707308; log|cos psi| = 9.9437847; their difference is 9.4269461.

Column 3 (B, b):
- cot B = cot Omega cos i · cos(psi+eps) / (cos psi cos eps): 9.4269461 + 0.0374833 (sec eps) + 9.9983017 (cos(psi+eps)) = 9.4627311.
- Hence B = 106°11'2.10".
- sin b = sin Omega cos eps / sin B: 9.9625167 + 9.9881674 + 0.0175606 = 9.9682447.

Column 4 (C, c):
- cot C = (same factor) · sin(psi+eps) / sin eps: 9.4269461 + 0.3999304 + 8.9457847 = 8.7726612.
- Hence C = 86°36'33.84".
- sin c = sin Omega sin eps / sin C: 9.6000696 + 9.9881674 + 0.0007609 = 9.5889979.

Controls:
- sin a is recomputed as cos i·sin Omega/|cos A|: 9.9966236 - 9.9998196 = 9.9968040.
- cos b and cos c come from the orthonormality identities cos b = sin a sin c sin(C-A) and cos c = sin a sin b sin(A-B):
  - 9.9968040 + 9.5700436 = 9.5668476 = log cos b;
  - 9.9968040 + 9.9677370 = 9.9645410 = log cos c.
  These agree with sqrt(1 - sin^2) and satisfy cos^2 a + cos^2 b + cos^2 c ≈ 1.
- Adding omega: A' = A + omega = 340°4'9.72"; B' = 252°50'20.34"; C' = 233°15'52.08".

Right block (conversion to eccentric anomaly), [mine] formula. Using r cos v = a(cos E - e) and r sin v = a sqrt(1-e^2) sin E:
- x = a sin a [sin A' cos E + sqrt(1-e^2) cos A' sin E] - a e sin a sin A' = R_x sin(E + phi_x) + K_x.
- R_x sin phi_x = a sin a sin A'; R_x cos phi_x = a sin a sqrt(1-e^2) cos A'.

Logs computed:
- log a sin a = 0.3691561; log a sin b = 0.3405968; log a sin c = 9.9613500.
- Each minus 0.0016584 (= -log sqrt(1-e^2)) gives 0.3674977, 0.3389384, 9.9596916.
- log sin and log cos of A', B', C': 9.5326035, 9.9731768; 9.9802213n, 9.4699074n; 9.9038519n, 9.7767900.
- Products: 9.9017596 and 0.3406745; 0.3208181n and 9.8088458n; 9.8652019n and 9.7364816n.
- log e = 8.9406312.

Results ('Zum Gebrauch'):
- x = [0.3676940] sin(E + 339°59'57.06") + 0.0695650
- y = [0.3404530] sin(E + 252°54'2.05") + 0.1825784
- z = [9.9607581] sin(E + 233°22'9.41") + 0.0639489
- Brackets denote logarithms. The constants are -a e sin a sin A', etc. (for example log = 8.9406312 + 9.9017596 = 8.8423908, giving 0.069565).
- Auxiliary logs 9.9729835 = log cos phi_x, 9.9803651 = log sin phi_y, 9.9044438 = log sin phi_z, used to obtain R.

Margins: 297 + 4 = 301 is a table-argument addition. The right-margin figures 1313, 3939 = 3·1313, 38077, 15, 104 are unexplained scratch.

(III) SOLAR PLACES.

May 12:
- Mean longitude for April 30, 37°50'37.10", plus 12 days of mean motion (12 × 3548.33" = 11°49'39.96") gives 49°40'17.06".
- Equation of centre +1°27'10.89", correction -1.06": 51°7'26.89".
- Perturbations +6.99 - 7.93 + 5.66 and constant reduction +37.03 give the true longitude L = 51°8'8.64".
- Radius: R = 1.0109675 + 133 - 154 + 123 (units of 1e-7) = 1.0109777, log R = 0.0047416.
- log cos L = 9.7975982; log sin L = 9.8913337; log R cos eps = 9.9672583; log R sin eps = 9.6048112, with eps = 23°27'49.75".
- X = R cos L = 0.6343659; Y = R cos eps sin L = 0.7220911; Z = R sin eps sin L = 0.3134331.

May 16:
- 37°50'37.10" + 15°46'13.28" = 53°36'50.38".
- +1°21'51.11" - 0.99" gives 54°58'40.50".
- +6.64 - 7.50 + 5.26 + 37.01 gives L = 54°59'21.91".
- R = 1.0117860, log 0.0050887.
- log cos L = 9.7587058; log sin L = 9.9133084; log R cos eps = 9.9676054; log R sin eps = 9.6051583, with eps = 23°27'49.69".
- X, Y, Z are not yet formed.
- The anomaly arguments (8612.77, 8722.27, 191/730/789/303, 327/736/799/303) add correctly.
errors: Column 4 writes log sin Omega as 9.9881694, but the sum giving log sin c = 9.5889979 uses 9.9881674. This is a copying slip (or misread digit) with no effect.

The final log amplitude for x is written 0.3676940 over an overwrite. Recomputing it from the page's own logs gives 0.3404530-analogue 0.3406745 - 9.9729835 = 0.3676910 (also 9.9017596 - log sin phi_x = 0.3676910). There is a possible slip of 3 units in the 7th decimal, which is negligible.

The 'n' (negative) marks in the right block are inconsistent with the signs actually used. sin(340°4') is negative but unmarked, cos(340°4') is positive but marked n, and cos(233°16') is negative but unmarked. The resulting phases and constants are nevertheless correct, so these are notation or transcription lapses.

Auxiliary angle psi: tan psi = tan i/cos Omega (log 9.7352639) gives 151°28'20.5", not the transcribed 151°28'10.48". The page's psi+eps = 174°56'10.48" is consistent with 151°28'20.5" + 23°27'49.98", so the error is in the reading or the copying, not in the computation used.
No substantive computational errors were found. A, B, C, the sines, the phases, the constants and the solar reductions all check to the last digit or two.

results.what: Second orbital elements of Vesta (1807), including the semi-major axis from Kepler's third law using the sidereal mean motion and Gauss's constant
results.modern_name: Preliminary orbit / osculating elements of (4) Vesta
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Vesta elements published in von Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz, 1807)

results.what: Reduction of Omega, i, eps to the constants sin a, A, sin b, B, sin c, C so that x = r sin a sin(A+u), etc., using an auxiliary angle psi with tan psi = tan i/cos Omega, plus orthonormality checks cos b = sin a sin c sin(C-A) and cos c = sin a sin b sin(A-B)
results.modern_name: Gaussian vectors P, Q (equatorial direction cosines of the orbital frame); Gauss constants

results.what: Equatorial coordinates written directly as R sin(E+phi) + K in the eccentric anomaly E, for ephemeris computation
results.modern_name: Rectangular coordinates via P,Q vectors: r = a(cos E - e)P + a sqrt(1-e^2) sin E Q

results.what: Solar longitude, radius vector and equatorial solar coordinates for 12 and 16 May 1807 from solar tables
results.modern_name: Geocentric solar coordinates from tables (von Zach type)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine computational astronomy, entirely in line with Gauss's well-documented 1807 work on Vesta. It uses the equatorial-constants method he later printed in Theoria Motus (1809). Nothing here is non-standard.

transcription_corrections: '151.28.10,48' should read 151°28'20.5" (auxiliary angle psi). It is required by tan psi = tan i/cos Omega and by the following 174°56'10.48" = psi + eps.
'178.10.55,47' should be 178°20'55.47" (tan psi2 = tan i cos Omega, log 8.4598129). 201°48'45.47" is then psi2 + eps.
'min [?] 9,9968040' is the label 'sin a' (log sin a).
'Sonnenferne' is the aphelion longitude; the perihelion is 249°58'9.10".
'Gr. Ax: 2,356961' is the semi-major axis itself (antilog of 0.3723521).
Column 4 '9,9881694' is most likely 9.9881674 (log sin Omega), as used in the sum.
The overwritten '0,3676940' in 'Zum Gebrauch' may be 0.3676910 in intent; the recomputed value is 0.3676910.
'Ψ =' at the left is an unfinished label.
